from_notes: Components: 1. Demand incentives: for e-2W, e-3W, e-ambulances, e-trucks, etc. 2. Grants for capital assets: e-buses, charging network, and the upgradation of testing agencies.
x: PM E-DRIVE (Ministry of Heavy Industries, ₹10,900 crore, from 1 Oct 2024) has two components: demand incentives for e-2W, e-3W, e-ambulances, e-trucks and other emerging EVs (A), and grants for capital assets – e-buses, the charging network and upgradation of testing agencies (C). It gives no grants for private EV manufacturing plants (B – that is the PLI route) and no tax rebates for buyers (D), so 'A and C only'.
source: PMF Environment 04 (src/environment/pmf-environment-04.txt) p.268; PMF LENS Aug 2026 (src/current-affairs/pmf-lens-2026-08-02.txt) p.130-131 (scope, ₹2,000 crore charging grant); psa.gov.in/press-releases/…/8818 (outlay ₹10,900 crore over two years); Rocket CA 2026 Part 01/02 checked – no PM E-DRIVE entry

from_notes: Third-Party Certification (NPOP): Implemented by Accredited Certification Agency under the National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP) of Ministry of Commerce and Industry ... APEDA acts as the secretariat for implementing NPOP.
x: Organic certification in India runs under the National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP) of the Ministry of Commerce, with APEDA as its secretariat (it accredits the certification agencies), so APEDA is the expected answer. FSSAI regulates the sale and labelling of food, BIS sets product standards and CSIR is a research body – none of them runs organic certification.
source: PMF LENS Jan 2026 (src/current-affairs/pmf-lens-2026-01-02.txt) p.29-30; app notes 6:36 sub 9 (APEDA runs NPOP); Rocket CA 2026 Part 01 p.87 (APEDA under Ministry of Commerce and Industry); FSSAI/BIS roles: general knowledge, not checked

from_notes: Outlay: ₹10,900 crore for implementation from Oct 2024 to Mar 2026.
x: The Cabinet approved PM E-DRIVE in September 2024 with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore over two years, of which ₹2,000 crore is for EV charging. ₹10,000 crore (the old key) was the FAME-II outlay; ₹2,000 crore is only the charging component and ₹5,000/₹20,000 crore have no source.
source: PMF Environment 04 (src/environment/pmf-environment-04.txt) p.268; psa.gov.in/press-releases/cabinet-approves-pm-electric-drive-revolution-innovative-vehicle-enhancement-pm/8818 (outlay Rs 10,900 crore over two years)

x: ₹2,000 crore was earmarked for EV charging infrastructure (about 72,300 fast chargers) under PM E-DRIVE, whose total outlay is ₹10,900 crore. ₹10,000 crore was the FAME-II outlay, not the charging allocation.
